subject: OrbitCloud SLA: uptime target & monthly credit amendment
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena.park@orbitcloud.com>
To: dylan_brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@orbitcloud.com
Date: 2027-04-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: SLA amendment request — availability floor and monthly remedy

Hi Dylan,

Thanks again for the demo last week. OrbitCloud legal and procurement have reviewed Redwood's standard SLA and we'd like to propose a couple of changes before we sign the Dedicated Capacity PO. High level:

- Request: reduce the guaranteed monthly availability floor for our dedicated cluster from the standard 99.95% to 99.9% for the first 6 months of the contract (we're onboarding high-traffic inference workloads and expect an initial tuning period).
- Remedy: increase the monthly service credit cap for availability shortfalls to a straight percentage of our committed spend (we'd like up to 50% of committed monthly fees for severe outages) rather than the fixed token-based buckets in your template.

We know these are non-standard asks. To help you evaluate, I attached a short incident summary of our recent launch (incidents_Q1-2027.csv) and a proposed amendment draft from procurement. Can you outline operational constraints and whether Redwood can accept this, or an acceptable alternative? We can loop in procurement and legal if you want to negotiate working-level details.

Best,
Elena
Elena Park
Head of Cloud Operations, OrbitCloud
elena.park@orbitcloud.com
Attachments: incidents_Q1-2027.csv
From: dylan_brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@orbitcloud.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-21T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLA amendment request — availability floor and monthly remedy

Hi Elena — thanks for the context and the file. I also appreciate OrbitCloud being upfront about the onboarding risk. Quick summary of Redwood's position after an internal ops + pricing pass:

- Availability floor: we generally hold to a 99.95% monthly availability guarantee for Dedicated pools. Dropping to 99.9% materially changes our capacity planning and risk exposure.

- Proposed compromise: temporary phased floor for the first 3 months (99.9%) tied to a playbook for a production readiness ramp (pre-warm strategy + traffic shaping). After the ramp period, the floor would revert to 99.95%.

- Monthly remedy: we can agree to a spend‑based remedy calculation (percentage of committed monthly fees) for severe outages, but we need a cap and an escalator model. Suggested model: up to 50% of committed fees for a severe availability window in a month, with a hard annual cap of 200% of one month's committed fee across all remedy events. This keeps the remedy proportional while bounding our long-term exposure.

- Maintenance carveouts and transient failovers: we'll carve out planned maintenance windows and short, infra-led failovers (<5m) if they meet our runbook criteria. Anything longer will be evaluated under the remedy model.

I've attached an editable amendment (SLA_Proposed_Amendment_v2.docx) that reflects the compromise above and maps to Redwood's operational constraints. Marissa (cc) and Ben are on-thread to comment on ops and commercial terms respectively.

If this looks reasonable, can we schedule a 30-minute working session next week to lock wording and get procurement on DocuSign?

Thanks,
Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: SLA_Proposed_Amendment_v2.docx
From: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@orbitcloud.com>, dylan_brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-22T11:32:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLA amendment request — availability floor and monthly remedy

Adding ops notes from a stability POV — happy to join the working session. A few operational clarifications to avoid surprises:

- Pre-warm & KV cache: for large model deployments we recommend a pre-warm job during the ramp. That mitigates the short-term latency increases and cold-KV cache misses that typically show up as availability dips in the first 48–72 hours.
- Regional failover: if OrbitCloud uses multi-region routing, some brief regional divergence can look like a customer-impacting outage in our telemetry; the remedy model should reference "customer-visible requests" rather than internal health checks.
- Measurement: availability will be measured at the API endpoint level (per-route, per-model) using our standard telemetry window. We can share a sample calc sheet in the working session so procurement has full visibility.

Operational ask: if we agree to a temporary 99.9% floor, I'd like a joint runbook and a list of rollout milestones that trigger re-evaluation back to 99.95% (e.g., error rate baseline, 14-day steady-state traffic). That helps ops triage and avoids surprise credits.

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
Customer Reliability Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Elena Park <elena.park@orbitcloud.com>
To: dylan_brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@orbitcloud.com
Date: 2027-04-25T10:24:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLA amendment request — availability floor and monthly remedy

Dylan / Marissa — thanks, this is helpful. Procurement reviewed your suggested compromise and the spend-based remedy model looks workable. A couple of practical next steps:

1) Please send a redline of SLA_Proposed_Amendment_v2.docx incorporating the Phase 1 (3-month) 99.9% floor, the 50% monthly cap language, and the annual hard cap language you proposed. We'll get procurement on the DocuSign flow once the redline is in place.
2) We'd like a 45-minute working session on Tue (04/27) to review the joint runbook and the availability measurement calc sheet. Can Marissa join?

If you can deliver the redline by Monday EOD, procurement will queue DocuSign. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Elena
